title: Discovery of new empirical laws, confirmed by experiment

concept.text: The proposed innovation is an ML system that formulates a compact, genuinely new quantitative law about a natural system, derives an observable consequence before the relevant measurement is available, and obtains independent experimental confirmation. The system would supply the substantive mathematical relationship and prediction. Its output would specify the quantities involved, underlying assumptions, applicable conditions, and expected uncertainty. Synthesis of the proposed capability.

The capability connects symbolic equation discovery, auditable novelty, prospective prediction, and physical experimentation. AI Feynman supplies an example of recovering mathematical expressions from numerical data and explicitly identifies discovery of previously unknown physics formulas as an aspiration. The AI Scientist demonstrates integration of several computational research stages. These foundations motivate the proposed empirical discovery loop, while their supplied demonstrations cover narrower achievements.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would demonstrate that ML can originate an empirically productive quantitative explanation and expose it to an independent prospective test. The immediate scientific contribution would be a law supported over the measured conditions and uncertainty range. Its importance would depend on the phenomenon explained, the prediction's discrimination among existing explanations, and the extent to which the relationship organizes observations into a compact account. This is a conditional significance judgment.

Existing algorithm discovery already contributes new knowledge. AlphaEvolve demonstrates evaluator-guided discovery with mathematical results and practical deployments, including evaluations involving physical hardware timings and deployed-system measurements. Automated evaluation can therefore have empirical contact. For this innovation, the decisive advance would be an auditable new law about a natural system with a successful prospective experimental test. Program representation, automation, and the availability of an evaluator do not independently determine whether that advance has occurred.

One successful prediction would provide bounded confirmation. Establishing a reliable discovery method would require repeated successes across further phenomena, including tests of failure conditions and domain boundaries. A self-directed research community would additionally require sustained problem selection, cumulative research, and reliable verification. Orders-of-magnitude acceleration across materials, drugs, and physics remains a conditional downstream possibility requiring many additional discoveries and effective experimental workflows. The supplied evidence supports a qualitative assessment of revolutionary significance, without a quantitative ranking against historical scientific advances. Synthesis of the impact and its limits.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability within the supplied demonstrations is reliable integration of four operations. A system must formulate a compact quantitative law, audit novelty against documented training and literature exposure, derive a discriminating observable consequence prospectively, and obtain independent experimental agreement within a stated domain and uncertainty. The reviewed examples establish selected equation recovery, automated ML experimentation, and evaluator-guided algorithm discovery. Their coverage leaves the broader field's achievement of this complete loop through 1 November 2026 unresolved.

Novelty auditing is a concrete technical barrier. A known formula can appear in an equivalent mathematical representation, and a search for the emitted expression alone can miss relevant prior exposure. A credible audit must address training data, retrieved literature, subsequent information, and equivalent formulations. The AI Scientist paper observes that typical public LLMs do not disclose their training data, which limits such checking. Recovering a known benchmark equation establishes equation-recovery performance while leaving originality and memorization questions open.

Scientific and engineering barriers also include selecting informative observables, handling measurement noise and uncertainty, identifying assumptions, and designing experiments that distinguish the proposed relationship from relevant existing explanations. Agreement on a measurement that all competing accounts already predict would provide limited evidence for a new law. Experimental execution must preserve the prospectively specified conditions and make discrepancies interpretable. These are synthesis-level requirements inferred from the proposed discovery task.

Connecting computational search to experiments introduces practical limits on evaluation speed and accessibility. AlphaEvolve explicitly excludes tasks requiring manual experimentation from its scope and acknowledges that only some natural-science experiments can be simulated or automated. The AI Scientist discusses physical-laboratory extensions as future work. A complete discovery system would need to accommodate experimental constraints and delayed feedback while retaining reliable prediction and evaluation.

current_state.text: Udrescu and Tegmark's AI Feynman paper, published in Science Advances on 15 April 2020 with an arXiv revision on the same date, reports recovery of all 100 selected equations from the Feynman Lectures on Physics using generated numerical data. The paper describes these basic equations as a training set for implementation and hyperparameter development. Its database includes known analytic expressions for answer checking. The result establishes recovery of selected known relationships under the benchmark conditions, with independent discovery and experimental confirmation of an unknown natural law remaining outside that demonstration.

Chris Lu, Cong Lu, Robert Lange, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, and David Ha presented The AI Scientist in an arXiv preprint submitted on 12 August 2024 and revised on 1 September 2024. It integrates idea generation, code generation, computational experiments, paper writing, and simulated review across diffusion modeling, transformer-based language modeling, and learning dynamics. These demonstrations concern automated ML research. The authors' description of earlier frontier models as performing only a small portion of science is a characterization from that period.

The AI Scientist abstract reports a cost below $15 per paper, while its experimental discussion gives approximate costs of $10–15 per paper. These figures are author-reported costs for the described workflow. They do not establish universal costs or independently certify the scientific quality of the generated papers. The body also describes substantial reliability limitations. Simulated review and computational ML experiments provide partial research automation, with independent experimental confirmation of a new natural-science law remaining outside the demonstrated scope. The supplied material identifies an arXiv preprint and establishes no subsequent journal-publication status.

The June 2025 AlphaEvolve arXiv paper documents LLM-directed evolutionary search grounded in code execution and automatic evaluation, with algorithmic discoveries and practical deployments. Its evaluation includes hardware timings and deployed-system measurements, illustrating that automated evaluators can measure physical performance. The paper explicitly excludes tasks requiring manual experimentation. These achievements establish relevant discovery machinery and a system-specific experimental boundary. They leave the proposed new-natural-law demonstration unestablished in the supplied evidence. Subsequent publication status is unspecified.

The supplied review had a complete AI Feynman paper extraction. The original research encountered a bot challenge at the Science Advances page, while the arXiv record supplied the journal reference. The retained AI Scientist extraction ends during Appendix C on page 40, and the AlphaEvolve extraction is truncated on page 36. The passages supporting the scope, costs, and limitations summarized here precede those truncations. Later appendix content falls outside the retained evidence.

The dated results establish relevant components across 2020, 2024, and 2025. Although the source index records retrieval on 9 November 2026, the supplied freshness-search record is empty. Consequently, this evidence cannot settle whether another system had completed the full empirical-law discovery loop by the review's 1 November 2026 cutoff. That coverage limitation leaves the historical demonstrations intact and the field-wide present status unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. Freeze and document all training data, literature exposure, retrieval sources, and subsequent information available to the system. Have the system emit a quantitative law with its variables, assumptions, domain of validity, and uncertainty claims. A mathematical statement fitting on one page is a proposed operational compactness threshold. Publish a novelty audit that searches relevant literature and documented exposure for equivalent formulations as well as matching expressions.
completion_criteria.label: One-page quantitative law with frozen exposure records and novelty audit

completion_criteria.text: Proposed prospective test. Before experimental results become available, register a quantitative prediction for a genuinely new physical measurement that distinguishes the proposed law from relevant existing explanations. An independent laboratory would conduct the measurement under a pre-registered protocol with an uncertainty budget, specified tolerance, and explicit conditions for interpreting success or failure. Initial success would require agreement within that registered tolerance.
completion_criteria.label: Preregistered novel measurement independently confirms prediction within registered tolerance

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirements. Release the dated law and prediction, experimental procedures and records, analysis methods, and reproducible corpus and literature searches. Independent replication should probe the original conditions and additional conditions within the claimed domain. Tests near proposed domain boundaries should help identify where the law ceases to apply. Repeated discoveries across further problems would provide evidence for a transferable discovery method.
completion_criteria.label: Released discovery records and independent replication across claimed conditions

completion_criteria.text: Interpretive boundaries of the proposal. Corpus and literature searches would provide auditable evidence about originality and possible memorization, with their completeness explicitly documented. Agreement in finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth within tested conditions. Absolute novelty and literal universal validity would remain beyond what those checks establish. Recovery of a textbook equation or success in an automated programming contest alone would leave the empirical discovery criteria unsatisfied. These thresholds are proposed evaluation choices.
completion_criteria.label: Explicitly documented limits of originality checks and experimental validation

related_concepts.text: MLC-06, Algorithmic legibility sufficient to verify and edit a model, concerns understanding and modifying a model's internal computation. MLC-08 concerns the externally testable law and prediction it produces. Legibility could help explain or audit the discovery procedure. MLC-07, Open-ended curricula that create externally verified new competencies, overlaps with choosing subsequent problems and developing research abilities over time. Repeated law discovery could become one competency in such a curriculum. The supplied roster gives titles without full definitions, so these are provisional distinctions and establish no necessary dependency.

MLC-04, World models that survive novel interventions, overlaps with predicting outcomes under changed physical conditions and identifying informative experiments. MLC-08 adds the particular output of an explicit quantitative law with prospective experimental support. MLC-09, Skill learning from scarce, irreversible, real-world outcomes, overlaps with learning under costly experimental feedback. Its title emphasizes acquisition of skills under constrained outcomes, while MLC-08 emphasizes a scientific relationship and its confirmation. These relationships are synthesis based on the supplied roster titles.

MLC-01, A predictive theory of what deep networks learn, addresses deep-network learning as the object of theory. MLC-08 could conceivably generate laws about learning itself, alongside laws in other empirical domains. MLC-10, Non-vacuous behavioral certificates at frontier scale, concerns guarantees about model behavior. An independently replicated scientific prediction provides empirical evidence over tested conditions, whereas a behavioral certificate concerns a specified guarantee. These concepts retain separate targets. Synthesis based on the supplied roster titles.

MLC-02, Domain learning at a human experience budget, and MLC-03, Cumulative learning without forgetting or loss of plasticity, concern efficient acquisition and sustained retention of capabilities. They could contribute to a productive scientific learner by reducing required experience and preserving knowledge across successive investigations. A confirmed law could be discovered without demonstrating either broader learning capability. Synthesis based on the supplied roster titles.

MLC-05, Local credit assignment that matches backpropagation at scale, concerns the learning mechanism. MLC-11, Frontier competence at a biological-order power budget, concerns computational energy efficiency. Either could affect the cost or implementation of scientific discovery systems. MLC-08's proposed demonstration specifies a scientific output and experimental result, leaving learning architecture and power budget open. Synthesis based on the supplied roster titles.

Symbolic regression, automated research, experimental design, laboratory automation, and algorithm discovery are methodological overlaps. AI Feynman contributes expression recovery, The AI Scientist contributes integrated computational research, and AlphaEvolve contributes evaluator-guided search. Combining such components with a novelty audit and an independent prospective experiment motivates MLC-08, while each existing demonstration retains its own documented scope.

unresolved_issues: Whether any system completed the full empirical-law discovery loop by 1 November 2026 remains unresolved because no freshness-search record was supplied.
Absolute novelty and complete exclusion of memorization remain difficult to establish, especially when training data or other information exposure are unavailable.
The one-page compactness threshold, experimental tolerance, replication breadth, and required diversity of discoveries remain proposed choices requiring domain-specific justification.
The full definitions of MLC-06, MLC-07, and the other roster entries were unavailable. Their relationships are inferred from titles and the supplied discussion.

No review recommendation was rejected. Recommendations concerning scientific integration and experimental design were adopted as labeled proposals or synthesis.

brief.title: AI discovery of new laws of nature tested in a lab
possible: Scientists could use AI to propose a new law of nature: a short equation explaining how measurable quantities relate. It would predict a result before anyone measures it, and an independent laboratory would test that prediction.
why: Scientists would gain a compact explanation that connects observations and makes testable predictions. AI would contribute the mathematical relationship itself, extending its role in discovering how nature works.

sources.showed: AlphaEvolve discovered new algorithms and improved parts of Google's computing systems. It tested candidates automatically.
sources.quote:
Furthermore, AlphaEvolve discovered
novel, provably correct algorithms that surpass state-of-the-art solutions on a spectrum of problems
in mathematics and computer science,
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates automated discovery guided by tests of proposed solutions.
sources.not_established: It did not demonstrate a new law of nature confirmed independently, and its scope excludes experiments requiring manual work.

sources.showed: AI Feynman recovered all 100 selected textbook equations from generated numerical data.
sources.quote:
We apply it to 100 equations from the Feynman Lectures on Physics,
and it discovers all of them,
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates that software can recover compact equations from numerical data.
sources.not_established: Recovering known equations does not establish discovery of an unknown law or confirmation through a new experiment.

sources.who: Chris Lu, Cong Lu, Robert Tjarko Lange, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune and David Ha
sources.showed: The AI Scientist combined idea generation, coding, computer experiments, paper writing and automated review in machine learning, where computers learn from data. The preprint reports substantial reliability limitations.
sources.quote:
We demonstrate
the versatility of this approach by applying it to three distinct subfields of machine learning: diffusion
modeling, transformer-based language modeling, and learning dynamics.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates integration of several stages of computational research.
sources.not_established: It did not demonstrate independent laboratory confirmation of a newly discovered law of nature.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate pieces of the task. Udrescu and Tegmark recovered known physics equations. Google DeepMind discovered algorithms through automated testing. The AI Scientist team linked research ideas to computer experiments and written reports.
missing: A complete demonstration would need an AI-authored law with clear assumptions, conditions and uncertainty.
An originality check would need to cover what the system had seen, including equivalent forms of known equations.
An independent experiment would need to confirm a prediction made in advance that distinguishes the law from existing explanations.
Independent repeats would need to establish where the law works and where it fails.

milestones.label: A compact law passes a documented originality check
milestones.explanation: A one-page law would state its quantities, assumptions, scope and uncertainty, with frozen records of all information exposure and searches for equivalent formulas. This would make its originality assessable.

milestones.label: An independent measurement confirms a prediction registered in advance
milestones.explanation: An independent lab would test a new measurement under an advance protocol covering uncertainty and success limits. Agreement within those limits would support a prediction that distinguishes the law from existing explanations.

milestones.label: Public discovery records support independent repeat experiments
milestones.explanation: Released discovery and experiment records would support independent repeats across claimed conditions and near boundaries. These would test its scope; discoveries on further problems would test whether the method transfers.

milestones.label: Originality and experimental claims have explicit limits
milestones.explanation: Reports would state how complete originality checks are and which conditions experiments cover. This would bound claims: searches cannot prove absolute novelty, and finite tests cannot prove a law holds everywhere.

uncertain: Hidden training data and equivalent formulas make it difficult to rule out memorization completely.
The proposed page limit, acceptable prediction error and breadth of repeat experiments need justification for each scientific field.
A successful discovery would leave open whether the method can reliably discover laws across other phenomena.

page.title: Machine discovery of new empirical laws
page.definition: A machine-learning system formulates a previously unknown equation relating measurable properties of a natural system and predicts a new measurement. An independent laboratory confirms the prediction under stated conditions and measurement uncertainties.

goal.need: Choosing which materials to make can require testing far more compositions than a laboratory can synthesize. One search for water-splitting catalysts had 3,545 candidate oxides. Common predictors require calculations of electronic properties that are uncertain at the catalyst surface. Discovering which combination of ionic radii predicts activity lets electrochemists rank candidates before synthesis. They still need to check which materials form the intended crystal structure: only five of 13 selected compositions yielded a pure perovskite.

completion.title: An independent laboratory confirms a prospective prediction of a new ML-discovered empirical law.
completion.criterion: An ML system supplies a quantitative relationship for a natural system that peer-reviewed assessment finds absent from prior literature. It specifies variables and conditions and yields a quantitative prediction dated before measurement. A first prospective physical experiment supports it; a separate laboratory then collects new data and confirms a prospectively specified prediction of the same relationship under the test protocol's uncertainty model and acceptance criterion. Reports identify the system's mathematical contribution and distinguish confirmation data from discovery data.
completion.set_by: Atlas operational criterion; no external body was found to have published this combined test.
completion.basis: Searched the Turing challenge report, DARPA's autonomous-scientist goals, SRBench, SciLaws-Bench and laboratory equation-discovery papers. No combined criterion for ML authorship, law novelty and independent prospective physical confirmation was found. This Atlas test operationalizes the quoted goal; the National Academies' replication definition supplies the distinction between reanalysis and confirmation using new data.

milestones.title: An ML equation matches a known law up to an additive or nonzero multiplicative constant.
milestones.criterion: For a known nonconstant target equation f, simplify the candidate expression g symbolically. It passes if g is nonconstant and either f − g simplifies to a constant or f/g simplifies to a nonzero constant.
milestones.set_by: La Cava and colleagues, SRBench, Definition 4.1, published in the NeurIPS 2021 proceedings.
milestones.threshold_quote: This definition is designed to capture models that differ from the true model by a constant or scalar.

milestones.title: A symbolic-regression system recovers a double pendulum's Hamiltonian from measured motion.
milestones.criterion: Recover the double pendulum’s Hamiltonian, the expression for its conserved energy, from measured angles and angular velocities. Compare candidate equations by their number of terms and their error in predicting pairs of partial derivatives on withheld motion data. Select the simplest equation at the largest gain in predictive ability.
milestones.set_by: Schmidt and Lipson, Science, 2009; their published laboratory demonstration and equation-selection procedure. This is a study-specific test.
milestones.threshold_quote: the simplest equation with the largest increase in predictive ability.

milestones.title: An ML-discovered new empirical law passes its first prospective physical experiment.
milestones.criterion: An ML system supplies a quantitative relationship judged new relative to prior literature. Before the originating team takes a new physical measurement, it specifies the equation’s prediction, test conditions, uncertainty model and acceptance criterion. The measurement meets that criterion.
milestones.set_by: Atlas operational criterion. Searches of the Turing and DARPA goals, SRBench, SciLaws-Bench and laboratory equation-discovery studies found no external criterion for this first prospective confirmation.

milestones.title: Machine-derived equations for voltammetric peaks agree with a chemist’s analysis within experimental error.
milestones.criterion: Vary pulse height from 10 to 40 mV in 5 mV steps in differential pulse voltammetry. From the measured current, infer how each cadmium, lead and copper peak’s position and height depend on pulse height. Compare the inferred regularities with a chemist’s analysis of the same measurements using the experimental error estimated from repeat measurements.
milestones.set_by: Żytkow, Zhu and Hussam’s FAHRENHEIT laboratory protocol and accuracy comparison, 1990.
milestones.threshold_quote: both the maxima and regularities which are equivalent within empirical error

milestones.title: A model earns the full structure score of 1 on a hidden SciLaws-Parallel equation.
milestones.criterion: Starting with the public task information and no observations, query the simulator within the task’s input ranges and query budget. Submit an equation that the protocol judge rates 1 for recovery of the complete hidden structure, including the changes to the published form. Algebraic equivalents count when coefficient signs and scales are consistent.
milestones.set_by: Huang and colleagues, SciLaws-Parallel structural-recovery protocol, Appendix C.5.
milestones.threshold_quote: full hidden-structure recovery up to algebraic equivalence with consistent coefficient signs and scales

not_found: No published demonstration combining a new ML-originated empirical law with independent prospective physical confirmation was identified in the searched literature.

results.finding: AI Feynman exactly recovered 100% of 100 known equations from the Feynman Lectures on Physics.
results.detail: The authors tuned the algorithm on the 100 basic equations and selected and analyzed the 20 bonus equations after finalizing the algorithm and its hyperparameters.
results.quote:
We apply it to 100 equations from the Feynman Lectures on Physics,
and it discovers all of them

results.finding: AI Feynman 2.0 recovered Einstein’s kinetic-energy law and solved 73 of 100 Feynman benchmark problems under added Gaussian noise.
results.detail: The exact recovery in Figure 1 establishes the symbolic match. The 73-of-100 result is a separate benchmark total.
results.quote:
Convex corners reveal particularly useful formulas, in this case Einstein’s formula and
the classical approximationmv2/2.

results.finding: Across 4 physical systems, symbolic regression recovered exact known laws, corresponding to a symbolic difference of 0 on the same scale.
results.detail: The constant difference and ratio follow from the reported exact recovery and normalization. The article gives no separate symbolic simplification trace.

In all of our

results.finding: For 1 physical double pendulum, the Hamiltonian was the simplest equation at the largest predictive gain among about 10 candidates.
results.detail: High-energy data alone favored approximate angular-momentum conservation. Low-velocity data alone favored small-angle approximations and uncoupled energy terms. The combined data yielded the Hamiltonian.
